lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits.

Fall's leaves on Windows are answered. Decision 266. The hosted Windows machine drew fall at rest through Direct3D 11, and the still was read back here with the head and the sha256 its builder stated. Measured here against the two Linux stills: in the 15,205 pixels where the text on the main branch and the dropped rewrite differ, the Windows picture is nearer the main branch's in 14,268, nearer the rewrite in 816 and at the same distance in 121; where the two differ by 8 levels or more, 6,061 of 6,062 are nearer the main branch's. The whole Windows still stands 40.90 dB from the Linux guard, inside the handoff's floor of 39 dB. Seen in a cut at four times, the first picture attached: the large leaf carries its midrib and its fold's shading on Windows as on Linux, and is one flat colour in the rewrite. The hold on the release line for this picture is lifted; the line itself stays off until the freeze and his word. A real graphics card is still unknown.

Summer's fireflies, open item 276: the first commit is taken for chain 44. Decision 266. Its report came at 9:13 PM MT Friday and was read whole here, its four pictures looked at. Stated and measured by its builder: four files, the whole test run 1065 passed and 8 skipped, seven guard stills equal to the list in force and summer just landed moving on purpose. Seen here in the second picture attached, film frame 1440 at 3840 at seven places: on the main branch each light is a band of two to four lines or a slab with a square end, and with the mend each is one streak. Logged open under the same item: a wedge at the first place, a faint second line at the seventh, and the lights still about 20 levels under the approved picture's. The row of beads in the lawn is the lawn's own blades standing in front of the light and is closed.

The proof at 3840 for that commit ran on four helper machines: film frames 1421 to 1429 and 1435 and 1436 at the masters' quality. All four stopped at their first frame because they never had the second software renderer's driver; they last drew on Wednesday under the first one. Ruled: the standard package is installed, and no machine's frame is taken before it prints the standard machine's calibration line (decision 147). Measured here on the standard machine and stated by each of the four as measured on its own: the same line on all five, the same package version on all five. A frame took between about 2.4 and 3.9 minutes there, as their lines state. At 9:36 PM MT all eleven frames were on origin and read back here with equal sha256. Decision 267. Measured here: the lights in the glass above the lawn rise from 91 at frame 1421 to 162 at frame 1429 and stand at 158 and 157 at frames 1435 and 1436, never dipping; their median width falls from 4.7 pixels to about 3.0 as the globe's own travel ends, the largest single step being 3.65 to 2.96 between frames 1425 and 1426; their median peak rises from 215 to 228. By a rough match the lights travel 45 to 65 pixels a frame, so a single light cannot be followed by its place. Seen here at full size, the third picture attached, and at three times, the fourth: no light is a row of beads, a band of lines or a bar as on the main branch, and from frame 1425 on every light is one slim streak. Two things are not attributed yet. In frames 1421 to 1424, while the globe itself still travels, lights lying across that travel are soft four cornered slabs. And about ten of the 1,406 pictures of a light carry a second stroke, a short hook at one end or a twin beside it. Whether these are new with the mend or the main branch's own cannot be told without the main branch's frames, so the four helpers each draw one frame of it, 1422, 1426, 1428 and 1436, ordered at 9:40 PM MT. The take into chain 44 stands unless that pair shows a fault that is new with the mend.

The render instructions for his own computer: the row for a failed test is in the file and pushed, stated by its builder at 9:31 PM MT. It says: render nothing, change no floor, do not run the test again, and it gives one sentence for Brandon to bring the folder into this thread. The test itself now leaves a folder on the Desktop named Snow Globe Seasons - Test - Failed with its report, the contact sheet and what the machine drew, and a passing test takes it away; measured in its builder's machine on a made up failing test. Its proof on hosted test machines is running and nothing of this head is proven there yet. A slip it reported and mended: a mistyped switch made the stamp tool begin to draw; it was stopped after seconds with nothing written, and the tool now refuses a switch it does not know. No final render is started in the cloud.

The stall's mend: the two sheets of the menu's states were looked at here after Status 245, and every state is the same as the main branch's. Floor 6, the point sprites on the merged tree and the menu's walk on the main branch, is due by 9:55 PM MT.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. Chain 44: the stall's mend with the point sprites, summer's fireflies (the pair with the main branch's frames, then the second commit on the lights' width, due by 10:50 PM MT) and the seeds' dots, the frost line at film frame 668 (report due about 10:35 PM MT), the Direct3D mend last (its last part due by 10:40 PM MT), as each passes. Then a critic for the change of season and a fifteenth publish. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code, then a cold read by a fresh critic. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard and BUILD COMPLETE.

Open, below the bar: summer's landing streaks whiter and coarser than approved and its base darker. Summer's pond at rest (item 279). Fall's storm paler than approved. Spring's glass after a shake pale on pale, with square corners at the lower ends of a few runs. Spring's fence and trails. The fireflies at 4K until chain 44, and after it their wedge, the faint second line and their brightness (item 276). The seeds' lumps of dots at the stills' close camera (item 277). The sand of the petals' mend at 4K before the encode, one small petal's softer edge and the petals' fringe at film frames 681 and 682 (item 278). The frost line at film frame 668 (item 275). The stall at low quality on a software renderer, until chain 44, and after it still at the menu's options. One compiler caution on Windows at fall's leaf cards (item 282). The square pressed fill of one menu option (item 283). One level in 14 corner pixels of the menu on a starved machine (item 284). Winter's four small items. Fall's near fence and the pumpkin's stepped face (item 272). The poster tool that stops on one failed request (item 273). Not verified: a real graphics card, a phone, Safari, Firefox, sound heard by a person.
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 07.
